en: The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Noble and Most Victorious Dhāraṇī,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court-Dispersing Grandee,
Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, and Dharma-Master Subject Shi Hu, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying in the country of Pāṭaliputra, in the great city of Śrāvastī, at the Jetavana Monastery.
When this summer retreat had passed, it was the twentieth day of the ninth month.
There was a bhikṣu named Vāhyakhaṇa. At that time,
the bhikṣu departed from the great city of Xingzuò and traveled to the city of Zhīnà, which was four yojanas away.
Along the way, he saw a great man three zhang tall and four chi wide in the face.
Recognizing him as the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, he immediately prostrated at his feet, knelt with palms joined, and addressed the Bodhisattva, saying:
"How is it that you have manifested your body and come here?
There must be a cause and condition.
The Bodhisattva replied, "So it is; so it is."
"O Bhikṣus, among all the sentient beings within this Jambudvīpa,
there shall be those who suffer from illness.
The asuras, garuḍas, and others dwell on one side of Sumeru, the king of mountains."
They engaged in mutual combat with the devas and humans;
consequently, the sun and moon lost their radiance in the void and the stars did not appear.
Once the devas and humans were defeated, the asuras emerged victorious.

At that time, various ghosts and spirits took advantage of this opportunity to transform themselves into the forms of women, harassing and disturbing living beings and causing them to contract various diseases,
such as headaches, abdominal pains, and ailments of the eyes, ears, and nose.
Or they may develop abscesses, carbuncles, scrofula, hemorrhoids, fistulas, scabies,
leprosy, sores, or ringworm; or again,
they may suffer from malaria, which recurs at intervals of one day, two days, three days, or four days.
Even all evil diseases such as wind-disorders, bile-fevers, and phlegm-accumulations;
furthermore, within Jambudvīpa, there shall be great winds and rains,
whether cold or hot, or excessive flooding or drought.
The five grains will not flourish, and the people, suffering from famine and scarcity, will all meet an untimely death.
Furthermore, beasts such as tigers, wolves, lions, and *mānava* will appear,
preying upon sentient beings and robbing them of their vital essence.
When these various difficulties came together to oppress and afflict him,
the Great Being, having explained this matter, addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"I possess a sacred and most supreme dhāraṇī."
Increasing one's roots of goodness can eliminate all evils.
Furthermore, if there is a person who gives rise to a pure mind and makes offerings of incense,
flowers, and so forth to the Triple Gem and the various worthies and sages.
If one maintains purity and observes the fast for seven days and nights while reciting this dhāraṇī, all these various difficulties will be immediately eliminated.
The dhāraṇī is as follows: Namo bhagavate vimalamatigambhīrāya.
Ṛjitarāja tathāgata svadhātya hi māragariṭe vimarodyanśi ālagate ālagate svāhā namas sarvanivaraṇa.
NAVIŚKAMBHINĀSATTA ĀGATA SVĀHĀ | TADYATHĀ | HĪ MAHĪ MAHĀMAHĪ SVĀHĀ | NAMO GURUKĀRĀYA TATHĀGATĀYA | TADYATHĀ | Ā...
gaṇāgare gaṇasvabhāve gaṇakīrtite svāhā | namo samantabuddhānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ svadhānyathā samaye svāhā ||
Homage! Namo aparājita-gamine | Tadyathā | gata svāhā | Tadyathā | amāmahi svāhā | Namo manaḥsantāpa svasthagata svāhā.
Nye tha ma na vi śuddhe padme śvare padma-sambhave kiṅkarihi dākārye svāhā | Namaḥ sarva-buddha-bodhisattvebhyaḥ ||
Oṃ namo ārya-mañjuśriye tadyathā | jaye jaye lamedi he mahe mahāmahe svāhā | namo ārya... [etc.]
Oṃ āvālokiteśvara-sarvadharmasvabhāva-śuddha-tattvāya tadyathā gaganatate gaganasambhave gaganamudre gaganavikrānti.
Hrīḥ svāhā. Namo 'rya-samantabhadra-tathāgatāya. Tadyathā: hrīḥ bhadre mahābhadre amale...
Namaḥ samantavighnāntakarājasya mahāvighnāntakarājasya svāhā | Namaḥ aryavīramatī-tathāgatāya anucirite ||
*Ta-sarva-jñi-vajra-svabhāva-vajra-nirdeśa-svāhā namo sarva-buddha-bodhisattvānāṃ tadyathā*
Kheṭakāranivaraṇīye svāhā | Jambhani stambhani mohani pāṇḍarāya svāhā | Mohanandi-nandapanyaye svāhā.
Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ svāhā | Saṃtīrṇasavanyirvāpanye svāhā | Nūravinurīye svāhā ||
Namaḥ kumārarūpiṇe svāhā | Namaḥ pañcacīrakopadhānāya svāhā | Namaḥ ājāneyavilabdhanaye svāhā | Namaḥ dāntakariṇe svāhā ||
Haya-gīśapāṭanāya svāhā | Mṛga-rāja-hayāya svāhā | Sarva-karman-viśodhanāya svāhā ||
Svāhā! To all the Buddhas, svāhā! To the Yakṣas, svāhā! To the Bhūtas, svāhā! To the Abhūtās...
ĀḤ SVĀHĀ SARVA DUHKHA-PRAŚAMĀYA SVĀHĀ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī...
Having spoken this most supreme holy dhāraṇī, he addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"You all, relying upon the ritual rules of this True Dharma,
should daily with sincere devotion give rise to a pure mind."
Make offerings to seven bhikṣus and provide sustenance for the Triple Gem and all the worthy sages.
During the first watch of the night, perform homa by kindling a fire;
this will eliminate calamities and cause them to quickly dissipate.
If there are good men or good women who receive,
uphold, read, recite, and extensively explain this True Dharma for others,
all their various illnesses shall be healed and cured.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen attentively now to this most excellent holy dhāraṇī."
Possessing the power of great illumination, it brings vast benefit to sentient beings.
It circulates everywhere throughout all the kingdoms, cities, towns, and villages of Jambudvīpa,
causing all sentient beings to hear, receive, and uphold it.
If a son or daughter of good family can read and recite this sutra even once,
their own physical illness and suffering will be swiftly healed.
If one recites it twice,
all illnesses and sufferings of one’s wife, children, and grandchildren shall be completely healed.
If one recites it three times, [the same shall occur].
All illnesses and sufferings of one's entire retinue shall be completely healed.
If it is recited four times,
all illnesses and sufferings of the people of an entire nation shall be completely healed.
If one recites it five times,
all the people within the borders of the king’s realm and in all the minor kingdoms shall obtain peace and happiness and be free from all diseases.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva said:
"Now, this True Dharma brings about vast benefit and is most rare;
quickly propagate it so that all sentient beings may obtain supreme merit."
If one gives rise to contempt for this sutra in one's mind,
and does not accept, uphold, read, or recite it,
nor expound or propagate it for others.
If any sentient beings within the boundaries of the kingdom do not obtain the opportunity to hear [this teaching],
those people will incur a transgression equal to the five heinous crimes.
Therefore, bhikṣus, you should with faith and reverence accept, uphold, and never forget this most supreme noble dhāraṇī.
As for those who dwell on one side of that King of Mountains, Sumeru:
"O gods, asuras, gandharvas, and others:
I have tamed myself so that the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa may attain great peace and happiness.
When Mañjuśrī had spoken this Dharma, he suddenly vanished.
When the bhikṣu Vākyakara heard what had been said, his heart was filled with great joy;
he accepted it with faith and practiced accordingly.
Thus concludes the *Buddhabhāṣita-ārya-paramavijayā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*.
